title: Btw I know they updated some of the jokes in the London revival, but ...
transcript: should we still be doing Avenue Q today or has it aged too poorly? I've heard this question come up a couple times recently and let's talk about it. my opinion and I'm open to hearing other takes on this is that it could probably benefit from another revision of the book partly just to update some of the jokes and references for modern times I know they did some of that but maybe a more holistic revision might be in order too but also yeah there are some elements that are maybe a bit problematic we can probably take another look at Christmas Eve and Lucy and little lines and moments here and there throughout the show and of course the song that gets brought up probably most often in this conversation Everyone’s A Little Bit Raclst listening to this song in 2026 is kind of fascinating because there is a generous read of this song as having a kernel of w*keness somewhere at its core because yeah we all grew up in this world with implicit biases and there are parts of this song that I think are trying to say that while it's tempting to ignore these prejudices out of fear of being labelled a bad person it's ultimately better to acknowledge them and with a revision there could still be a modern point to be made that feels in the spirit of the original song maybe about purity culture being unconstructive and the kind kind of “gotcha” activism that dominates a lot of conversations around political correctness but the song stops just short of these insights and ends up undermining them with an attitude that's probably a little too casually dismissive of these issues and maybe more importantly kinda shows a poor understanding of them And I know some people are gonna say the whole point is that it's shocking and uncomfortable stop with the w*ke over sensitivity yada yada yada but while there definitely is some shock value humor in Avenue Q ultimately it's not Family Guy it's not South Park trying to constantly push the line as much as possible The ethos of the show the central theme is life lessons some of which are very funny yes but I don't think they work dramatically or comedically if they don't ring true to our understanding of how the world work with something genuine large or small to take away from it. so yes, I do think it's possible to update some of this stuff without compromising the integrity of the material and I would argue that it's worth doing rather than shelving this show forever which I think would be throwing the baby out with the bath water because I've always found Avenue Q actually kind of beautiful even in its crass and goofy comedy I think there's an enduring relevance and relatability to this central idea reminding us through the Sesame Street format that we're never too old for life lessons that help us through the growing pains of living in the real world as an adult a premise that really hasn't aged at all
